summary: OpenSSH on Windows defaults to cmd.exe, but powershell.exe is recommended as better tested and faster. Change it via the HKLM:\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH DefaultShell registry value with PowerShell or win_regedit, and use meta: reset_connection so later tasks use the new shell.
questions: How do I change the default SSH shell on Windows to PowerShell?
Do I need to restart sshd after changing DefaultShell?
Can Ansible change the Windows OpenSSH default shell itself?
Why should I use reset_connection after changing the SSH shell?
How do I revert the Windows SSH shell to cmd?

answer_card.title: Changing the default SSH shell on Windows
answer_card.answer_md:
OpenSSH on Windows uses `cmd.exe` by default. `powershell.exe` is recommended because it's better tested and faster.

With PowerShell:

```powershell
# Set default to powershell.exe
New-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH -Name DefaultShell `
  -Value C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -PropertyType String -Force

# Set default back to cmd.exe
Remove-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH -Name DefaultShell
```

No `sshd` restart is needed; it applies to the next connection. With Ansible:

```yaml
- name: set the default shell to PowerShell
  ansible.windows.win_regedit:
    path: HKLM:\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH
    name: DefaultShell
    data: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
    type: string
    state: present

- name: reset SSH connection after shell change
  ansible.builtin.meta: reset_connection
```

`meta: reset_connection` makes sure the following tasks use the new shell.
